steps.text: Our dashboard uses last click. Using the sample journeys, how wrong is that, and which model gets closest to the truth?

On the sample, last click is the least accurate of the five models. Its channel shares are off from the true shares by 16 percentage points on average, which is roughly three times the error of the best model.

**Where last click goes wrong** (1,820 conversions; share of credit):

| Channel | Last click | True share | Last-click error | Conversions: last click vs true |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| display | 5.4% | 32.7% | **−27.3 pp** | 98 vs ~595 |
| paid_social | 6.0% | 25.3% | **−19.3 pp** | 109 vs ~461 |
| paid_search | 16.8% | 18.0% | −1.2 pp | 305 vs ~327 |
| email | 26.5% | 12.2% | **+14.3 pp** | 483 vs ~222 |
| organic_search | 17.9% | 9.4% | +8.5 pp | 326 vs ~172 |
| direct | 27.4% | 2.4% | **+25.1 pp** | 499 vs ~43 |

Last click gives direct about 11 times its real contribution and gives display about a sixth of its real contribution. Display and paid_social start most journeys. Direct and email tend to close them, so last click gives the closing channels the credit. Only paid_search is about right.

**Average error per channel, best to worst:**
1. **First touch: 5.2 pp** (closest)
2. Linear: 6.3 pp
3. Shapley: 6.3 pp
4. Markov: 8.0 pp
5. Last touch: 15.9 pp

**What to keep in mind:**
- **First touch only wins here because of how the sample was built.** It still has clear errors: display is 8 pp too high and email is 10 pp too low. Linear and Shapley are almost as accurate and spread credit more evenly, so I'd treat them as the safer defaults.
- **This is simulated data, not yours.** The "true share" exists only because a simulator generated these journeys. The simulator picks the middle touches of each journey at random, which works against Markov. On real data the ranking could be different, and your own journeys have no true share to check against.
- **None of these models measures what a channel actually adds.** They only divide up credit. To find out what display or direct really contributes, run a holdout test where some users don't see the channel. I can work out the sample size for one.

If you export your real journey paths, I can run the same comparison on them. There'll be no true share to score against, but you'll see how far your last-click numbers are from the other models.
